history.summary: Sri Uma Ramalingeswara Swamy Vari Devasthanam is a small neighborhood Shiva temple in the Jampeta/Hukumpeta area of Rajahmundry, listed in shaivam.org's East Godavari Shiva-temple directory and on Justdial (Aditya Nagar, Hukumpeta, 533107) and top-rated.online (Jampet, Rajamahendravaram 533104). It is NOT the Sri Ramalingeswara Swamy Vari Devasthanam of Yanamalakuduru hill, Vijayawada (CSV seq 14, already covered) - the 'Uma' prefix and Rajahmundry location distinguish it. No detailed history, founding date, or festival calendar is published online for this specific shrine; it appears to be a modern community temple with a daily 6 AM-8 PM schedule per Justdial. Identity is grounded by the map POI (Uma Rama Lingeswara Temple, Central Jail Road, Jampeta, 533103) matching the CSV name and town. CSV town 'Rajahmundry' is correct; locality is Jampeta/Hukumpeta within the city. FLAG: media is empty - two image searches returned only unrelated temples (Bugga Ramalingeswara Tadipatri, Umakotilingeswara Rajahmundry, Uma Maheswara Umamaheswaram), so no reliable image of this specific shrine was found.

town_description: Rajahmundry (officially Rajamahendravaram) is a historic city on the eastern bank of the Godavari River in coastal Andhra Pradesh, often called the cultural capital of the state. Founded around the 11th century by the Eastern Chalukyas (Raja Raja Narendra), it was the first capital of the Eastern Chalukya dynasty and later the birthplace of the Telugu language's classical literature. Today it is a major rail and road hub with its own airport, and its river ghats (Gowthami, Pushkar) are among the busiest pilgrimage spots on the Godavari.
